A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same research work, with readable text, equations, figures, tables, and complete Appendices A–F. The material supports a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original Gaussian-mixture simulations, ImageNet generation and composition experiments, and text-to-image results, including supplementary analyses in the appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results in Sections 3 and 5–6 and Appendices A–D, with one revised accuracy entry in Table 2.

M1.justification: The SEM-to-DLC encoding, DLC-conditioned DiT, SEDD generation and remasking, token composition, and LLaDA text-to-DLC procedures are unchanged. The introductory rewording does not modify the method.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same Gaussian-mixture simulations, ImageNet generation and composition tasks, and LAION image-caption training data. The text-to-image prompts and appendix test scenarios are also unchanged.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in Tables 1–3 and the qualitative comparisons, including Stable Diffusion with IP-Adapter in Appendix B. The added Pernias et al. citation is related work, not a newly evaluated baseline.

E3.justification: The reported data budgets, model configurations, training and sampling settings, evaluation metrics, guidance controls, and nearest-neighbor procedures remain unchanged in the main text and Appendix E.

E4.justification: Both retain the sequence-length and model-size analyses in Figure 5, remasking sensitivity in Appendix A, Stable Diffusion case study in Appendix B, Gaussian-mixture analysis in Appendix C, and novelty checks in Appendix D.

E5.justification: Table 3 retains the same mean-and-standard-deviation reporting across 10 randomly chosen image-embedding pairs. No run counts, seeds, uncertainty estimates, or statistical testing procedures are added or revised.

E6.justification: Table 2 changes DLC512 linear-probe accuracy from 84.8% to 85.3% under the same described evaluation. Its generative FID of 4.21 and encoding-decoding FID of 4.09 remain unchanged, as do other results and rankings. The PDFs do not explain the numerical revision.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and Equations (1)–(5), including the latent-code factorization, remasking posterior, and training objectives, are unchanged. No formal assumptions, theorems, or proofs are added or removed.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about unconditional ImageNet fidelity, compositional generation, and connecting pretrained language models to image generation through DLCs.

C2.justification: Interpretations concerning multimodal continuous distributions, representation structure, composition, remasking, and out-of-distribution novelty are unchanged. The appendices retain the same qualifications and failure explanations.

D1.justification: The implementation descriptions, hyperparameter Tables 4–6, hardware and training-time information, code link, and asset sources and licenses in Appendix F are unchanged. No new reproducibility details explain the revised accuracy.

R1.justification: Section 4 adds Pernias et al. (2023), Wuerstchen, to prior work conditioning diffusion models on image embeddings, with a corresponding bibliography entry. The broader positioning and novelty distinctions remain unchanged.

P1.justification: The introduction clarifies DLC conditioning and describes SEMs as distributions learned through SSL rather than calling SEM an SSL method. A Figure 5 typo is corrected, and the preprint footer becomes a NeurIPS 2025 footer. Section and appendix organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Figure 5 receives a caption typo correction, the publication footer changes, and the added reference causes limited bibliography reflow. Figures 1–12 and Tables 1–7 retain their designs and placement; Table 2's numerical revision does not redesign the table.

improvement.justification: v3 modestly improves explanatory precision in the introduction and acknowledges an additional relevant predecessor in Section 4. These provide limited gains in clarity and attribution. The scientific evidence and appendices remain essentially unchanged, and the unexplained Table 2 accuracy revision does not itself establish improved empirical reliability.
